segments.sub: A private place for a family's life, with a source for every fact.
segments.say: This is My Graph: | a private place for a family's life. | The people in it, what's coming up, | and where every fact came from. | In the next fifteen minutes, we'll walk through all of it, with the demo family: | Anna and Mikkel, and their children, Emma and Noah.

segments.title: What My Graph is
segments.sub: A private brain per graph, with a source for every fact.
segments.say: First, what My Graph is.

segments.title: Every fact has a source.

points.t: A small number marks each source
The exact words, and how sure

segments.say: My Graph keeps a graph: | the people in your life, the places, the events and the documents, | and how they connect. | Here is Emma's page. | Under What we know, every line is a fact, | and every fact carries a small cobalt number: its source. | Emma is Anna's child, | and the source is a line in a school letter. | Open a fact, and you see the exact words, | the document they came from, | and how sure the assistant was.

segments.title: Who said so, and what changed.

points.t: Everyone who told the graph about her

segments.say: On the right, Where Emma came from tells you how she entered the graph: | added by hand, as a family member. | Who said so lists everyone and everything that told the graph about her, | and how often. | And What changed keeps her history, | each change linked to the proposal it came from.

sub.t: A fact the assistant only inferred is marked as a guess, and stays a guess until a person confirms it.

segments.say: Each graph is its own private brain, kept in the family's own database. | Nothing in it is guessed silently. | A fact the assistant only inferred is marked as a guess, | and it stays a guess until a person confirms it.

segments.title: Graphs and sharing
segments.sub: Family, Work, a graph for two, and things that live in more than one.
segments.say: Graphs, and sharing.

segments.title: Separate graphs, for separate parts of life.

points.t: For Sara: shared with one person

segments.say: Anna has four graphs. | Family is the household's graph: | four people work in it, | and each person's private things stay their own. | Work is hers alone, and so is Personal. | For Sara is a graph she shares with one other person. | Share a graph, and the other person sees that graph, | and nothing from the others.

segments.title: One switch, and everything follows.

points.t: Today, people, library and chats follow

segments.say: The switcher at the top of the left rail moves between them. | Everything follows: | Today, the people, the library, the conversations and the assistant | all work inside the graph you have open.

segments.title: Each graph starts from its own template.
segments.say: Here is Anna's work graph. | A work graph starts from its own template, | so its people are colleagues and managers, not family. | The assistant asks different questions here too, | like what you're still waiting for on a project.

segments.title: One thing, in more than one graph.

points.t: Share a copy, with the details you tick
Or connect it with the same one
Changes on one side are proposed on the other
points.sync: the other side gets a proposal

segments.say: Some things belong in more than one graph. | Under Also in, you can share a person or a place into another graph, | choosing which details go with it, | or connect it with the same one that's already there. | When a ticked detail changes on one side, | the other side gets a proposal, | and only people who are in both graphs see the link.

segments.title: Today
segments.sub: What needs you, and the week ahead.
segments.say: Today.

segments.title: The first screen of the day.

points.t: How the assistant works, in plain words
This week: a row per person
Whose day is busy, at a glance

segments.say: Today is the first screen. | The first time, it explains how the assistant works in this graph: | it answers with a link to where each answer came from, | and it never changes the graph without asking. | Below is This week: | a row per person, in their own colour, | with events and to-dos day by day. | A parent sees at a glance | whose week is busy.

segments.title: Ready when you are.

points.t: Today's brief, with a source on every line
Proposed changes and what needs you

segments.say: Today's brief is a few lines on what's coming up: | what to pack, sign or book, | with a link to where each point came from. | Ready when you are | offers questions that fit the week. | On the right: proposed changes, | and what needs you, like possible duplicates. | And To do lists every reminder by day, | each with the person it's for.

segments.title: Ask, the assistant
segments.sub: Answers from your own graph, with their sources.
segments.say: Ask: the assistant.

segments.title: Ask about anything you've saved.
segments.say: Ask is the assistant. | You can ask from anywhere: press the slash key, | or type into Ask anything, at the top of the rail. | An empty conversation starts with questions that fit this family, | like what's coming up for Emma this week, | or which permission slips still need a signature.

segments.title: It shows its work, and its sources.

points.t: What it did, step by step

segments.say: Every answer shows what the assistant did. | Here, asked who Emma's teacher is, | it worked for eleven seconds, in seven steps: | it searched the graph and read the documents. | The number after Ms. Karen Hansen is its source: | the second school letter. | Underneath, you see which model answered, | through mux, the household's own model gateway.

segments.title: It asks before it changes anything.

points.t: Nothing is added until you say so

segments.say: When the assistant wants to change something, it asks first. | This card proposes a reminder. | Approve it, deny it, | or always allow reminders from now on. | Nothing is added until you say so.

segments.title: When you ask, it reads the web too.

points.t: Each web page listed as a source
Tied to what the graph already knows

segments.say: Ask it to look something up, and it reads the web too. | Here it found the zoo's opening hours, | the address, and how to get there, | with each web page listed as a source. | And it tied that to the zoo trip that's already planned for Saturday.

segments.title: When it isn't sure, it asks.

points.t: A question back, not a guess

segments.say: When a request isn't clear, it asks instead of guessing. | Here, asked to add a reminder for the trip, | it found only a reminder for Thursday, | and asked whether you want one for today, and at what time. | Then it proposes the reminder, for you to approve or deny.

segments.title: Conversations are kept.

points.t: Long ones compact into a summary
Private to the person who asked

segments.say: Conversations are kept on the left, grouped by day, | so you can come back to an answer and its sources. | Pin the ones that matter, rename them, or search them. | A long conversation can be compacted into a summary. | And conversations are private to the person who asked.

segments.title: Live highlights and the model
segments.sub: It sees what you mean as you type, and learns how your world fits together.
segments.say: Live highlights, mentions, and how a graph sees the world.

segments.title: It reads along as you type.

points.t: Known things link to the graph

segments.say: As you type, the composer reads along and highlights what it recognises: | Emma, Bellahøj Pool, Grandma Birgit. | Things the graph already knows link to it. | New people, places and facts are marked as new, | and when you send, | they're added with your message as the source. | You can untick anything you don't want added.

segments.title: Type @ to mention something.

points.t: Works in chat, memory and the wiki

segments.say: Type the at sign to mention something by name. | The menu finds people, places and pages in this graph, | and a mention links the question, the memory or the wiki page to them, | so it shows up on their page too.

segments.title: How this graph sees the world.

points.t: Kinds and relations, from a template
Or describe your world in a few sentences

segments.say: Each graph also has its own idea of the world. | How this graph sees the world lists the kinds of things it knows, | and the relations between them. | Family started from the family template. | When the assistant reads something that doesn't fit, | it proposes a new kind or relation, with where it saw them, | and you decide. | You can also describe part of your world in a few sentences, | and it proposes what's missing.

segments.title: People
segments.sub: Everyone around you, and how they know you.
segments.say: People.

segments.title: Everyone around you, in circles.

points.t: Family in the middle, then outward
Needs you: the people to look in on

segments.say: People shows everyone around you, in circles: | family in the middle, | then close friends, school and daycare, care and health, | friends and neighbours. | A dot grows with recent contact, | and a dashed ring means it's been longer than usual since you were in touch. | On the right, Needs you: | Noah is feeling low, | and it's three months since Anna spoke to Sofie.

segments.title: One person, brought together.

points.t: Keeping in touch, in one click

segments.say: A profile brings one person together: | how they've been, | when you were last in touch, their next birthday, | and who can see them. | Log a call, a visit or a message in one click. | Relationships are grouped, family, school, care, | and each one shows where it came from.

segments.title: You are in every graph.

points.t: Your own page, at the centre

segments.say: You are in every graph yourself. | Anna's own page is the centre of her circles: | everyone else relates to you, | so the graph can say Emma's grandparent, or your manager, | instead of a list of names.

segments.title: How do they know you?

points.t: A relation, or your own words

segments.say: Adding someone starts with the question that matters: | how do they know you? | Pick a relation, or describe it in your own words, | and choose who can see them. | What you enter by hand is saved as a confirmed fact, added by you.

segments.title: Library
segments.sub: Letters, photos, recordings and mail, each read for people and dates.
segments.say: The library.

segments.title: Drop it in, or paste it.

points.t: Letters, scans, photos, voice memos, mail

segments.say: The library holds every letter, scan, photo, voice memo and email the family adds. | Drop files in, choose them, | or paste straight from the clipboard. | Before anything is added, you choose who can see it: | only you, the parents, or the whole family, | and you can mark it sensitive.

segments.title: Kept as it was, then read.

points.t: A document keeps its own date

segments.say: Each file is kept exactly as it was, | then read for the people, places and dates in it. | A letter keeps its own date: | Noah's dentist letter sits on the timeline on the day it was written, | not the day it was uploaded. | What the reading finds is proposed, | never added straight away.

segments.title: Mail, filed by conversation.

points.t: Single emails, a mailbox, or a zip

segments.say: Mail comes in as single emails, a mailbox file, or a zip of emails. | Here is Sara's school mailbox: | all three messages imported. | Each message is filed with the rest of its conversation, | so a back and forth with the school reads as one thread. | And every document keeps its own date: | this letter was written in March 2024, | so that's where it sits on the timeline.

segments.title: Timeline
segments.sub: What happened and what's coming, a lane per person.
segments.say: The timeline.

segments.title: A lane per person.

points.t: Events, reminders and documents in time

segments.say: The timeline puts it all in time: | a lane per person, in their colour. | Events, reminders and documents sit where they belong, | with today as a line down the middle. | Filter by person or by topic, | and zoom from a week to everything.

segments.title: The shape of the year.
segments.say: Zoom out to a year, and the shape of the family's year appears: | school starts, trips, birthdays, deadlines. | Click anything to see where it came from.

segments.title: Wiki and co-writing
segments.sub: The family's own pages, written together with the assistant.
segments.say: The wiki, and writing together.

segments.title: The family's own pages.

points.t: @mentions put a page on a profile

segments.say: The wiki is for the family's own pages: | plans, how-tos, notes from school and the doctor. | Pages are set in a reading type, because they're read, not scanned. | Mention someone with the at sign, | and the page shows up on their profile.

segments.title: Ask the assistant to write.

points.t: A new section, a rewrite, or the whole page
Only a draft until you accept

segments.say: Pages are written together. | Ask the assistant to write a new section, | rewrite what you selected, or update the whole page. | It reads only what you can see in this graph, and cites it. | Its text is highlighted, and stays a draft until you accept it. | Every edit is versioned and attributed, | and an earlier version is one click away.

segments.title: Changes and History
segments.say: Changes, and history.

segments.title: Proposals wait for you.

points.t: From the assistant, the library, the web, connections
Each says where it came from

segments.say: Nothing reaches the graph without a person. | What the assistant, the library, web research and connections want to change | waits under Changes, as a change set, | much like a branch in git. | Each one says where it came from, | and what it would add.

segments.title: Review, deliver, or drop.

points.t: Deliver the rest, or drop it all

segments.say: Open one to review it. | Here, the library read a note about the class's forest trip. | Every change shows its evidence: | the quote, the document, and how sure the reading was. | Untick what isn't ready, and deliver the rest. | Or drop the whole thing, and nothing in it reaches the graph.

segments.title: Everything that changed.
segments.say: History is the log: | everything that changed in the graph, newest first: | who changed what, from what to what, | and the proposal it came from. | On every page, Who said so answers the same question for one thing.

segments.title: Go back in time.

points.t: Bring back how things were, as a proposal

segments.say: Compare two moments to see what changed between them, | and bring back how things were: | as a proposal, of course. | Checkpoints name a moment, like before a big import, | so you can come back to it. | History is never rewritten.

sub.t: The assistant, imports, web research, connections and check-ins all propose. Only a person delivers.

segments.say: That's the rule everywhere in My Graph. | Agents propose. People decide. | The assistant, imports, web research, connections and check-ins all propose. | Only a person delivers.

segments.title: Memory and the Brain Keeper
segments.sub: What the assistant keeps in mind, and who looks after it.
segments.say: Memory, and the Brain Keeper.

segments.title: What the assistant remembers.
segments.say: Memory is what the assistant keeps in mind between chats: | family rules, preferences and notes. | Packed lunch must be nut-free on trip days. | The Brain Keeper looks after it: | when there's something new, it decides what's worth keeping, | merges repeats, and retires what's no longer true. | Anything found only in a document, a web page or an email | waits for a parent to confirm it. | The assistant never follows instructions written in a document.

segments.title: Automations, check-ins and recipes
segments.sub: What the assistant does on its own, and only ever suggests.
segments.say: Automations, check-ins and recipes.

segments.title: It checks in, and only suggests.

points.t: At most five suggestions a day

segments.say: Automations is what the assistant does on its own. | A check-in runs every hour, here from seven until eight. | It looks at new files, reminders due soon, birthdays this week, | and people you haven't been in touch with. | It's stricter when nobody is watching: | it never adds facts, shares anything, or messages anyone. | It only suggests, at most five suggestions a day.

segments.title: Automations and recipes.

points.t: On a schedule, or when something happens
Runs as you, sees only what you see

segments.say: Automations run on a schedule, | or when something happens, | like when a document mentions a vaccination. | Recipes are saved instructions you run again and again, | like a weekly family summary. | Each one runs as you, sees only what you can see, | and lands its suggestions in Waiting for you.

segments.title: Connections
segments.sub: Calendars and mail that arrive by themselves. Aula's messages are next.
segments.say: Connections.

segments.title: Dates and letters, by themselves.

points.t: A mailbox, from the folders you choose

segments.say: Connections bring dates and letters in by themselves: | a calendar link, a mailbox from the folders you choose, | and Aula, the school platform, | through the two calendar links Aula gives every parent. | What they bring is read as data, never as instructions, | and what's found waits for your approval. | Reading Aula's messages is coming next.

segments.title: Documents and design sets
segments.sub: Reports, slides and briefs drafted from the graph, with a source on every claim.
segments.say: Documents, and design sets.

segments.title: Documents from your graph.
segments.say: Documents are reports, one-pagers, slides, briefs and profiles | that the assistant drafts from what's in the graph, | with a source on every claim. | Here is a slide deck about Emma's autumn: | each line carries the number of its source, | and the slides take shape on the right. | Nothing is shared until you publish it.

segments.title: Design sets decide how they look.
segments.say: A design set decides how documents look: | the type, the colours and the layout. | Use the built-in one, or make your own. | Slides can be exported to PowerPoint, | so a deck made here can go to a meeting.

segments.title: Settings, languages and themes
segments.sub: English and Danish, light and dark, and who is in the family.
segments.say: Settings, languages, and themes.

segments.title: Your own settings.

points.t: Light, dark, or like your device

segments.say: Each person has their own settings. | Choose English or Danish, | light or dark, or follow the device, | and your time zone. | Dates are shown in your own language and time.

segments.title: Every screen, in Danish too.

points.t: The whole app, in both languages

segments.say: Here is Mikkel's view, in Danish. | The whole app is in both languages, | and the text the assistant writes for you, | briefs, summaries and suggestions, | is written in yours.

segments.title: Light and dark.

points.t: Same colours for the same people

segments.say: And in the dark, everything keeps its meaning: | each person keeps the same colour, | and sources stay cobalt.

segments.title: Who is in the family.
segments.say: Family settings is where the household is set up. | Owner, parent, child or guest: | each role sees and does what fits. | Parents look after the children's accounts, | and a guest's access can end on a date.

segments.title: The iPhone app
segments.sub: Today, Ask, People, Timeline and Library, in your pocket.
segments.say: The iPhone app.

segments.title: The same graph, in your pocket.
segments.say: My Graph has a native iPhone app, | signed in to the same graph. | Today shows what's waiting for a decision: approve, always allow, or deny. | Ask works as on the web, with its steps, sources and approval cards. | And People shows each person with their relations, and where each came from.

segments.title: Timeline, memory, and a widget.

points.t: The timeline, coming up and earlier
Save to My Graph from any app
Next up, on the home screen

segments.say: The timeline shows what's coming up and what came before, | and memory shows the family's rules, each with its source. | From any app, Share and then Save to My Graph | sends a letter or a photo to the library. | A widget shows what's next up on the home screen.

segments.title: Privacy and trust
segments.sub: Built for a family's own data, children's included.
segments.say: Finally, privacy and trust.

rows.t: Only me, parents, or the whole household, on every item
Someone you share one with sees nothing from the others
Passkeys, and parents approve new devices
Every call through the household's own gateway
Private topics stay on local models
Never taken from a document, page or email

segments.say: My Graph is private by design. | Every item says who can see it: | only you, the parents, or the whole household. | Someone you share a graph with sees nothing from the others. | Sign-in uses passkeys, and parents approve new devices. | Every model call goes through the household's own gateway, | and a private topic stays on local models. | And instructions are never taken from a document, a web page or an email.

segments.title: See who signed in, and from where.
segments.say: Security settings show your passkeys and the devices signed in, | and the audit log records what happened, and who did it. | The assistant only ever sees what the person asking is allowed to see.

segments.sub: Agents propose, people decide. Every fact has a source.
segments.say: That's My Graph. | A private brain for each part of your life, | where the assistant proposes and people decide, | and where every fact can tell you where it came from. | Thanks for watching.
